name: inventory
title: Inventory
description: Everything a player has, in one place: a collection of `reward` and nothing more. It renders the list the host gives it, in the host's order, and passes one reveal handler down to whichever reward is waiting. The case it exists to get right is the empty one, which is the first thing a new player sees: no rewards means `data-gs-empty="true"`, a designed empty state with a glyph and a line of copy rather than a blank rectangle, and "nothing here yet" in the accessible name. A real list when it has items, so a screen reader is told how many before reading them. Performs nothing: it does not fetch the collection, sort it, paginate it or claim anything.
docs: Pass `rewards` as the list, already in the order you want it; this component never sorts. Pass `onReveal` once for the whole collection and it reaches every reward, or set one per reward to override it. Pass `emptyLabel` to say something about your own game to a player with nothing yet; the accessible name keeps the contract's "nothing here yet" whatever the copy says, so a test and a screen reader agree across every host. It brings `reward` with it, and both install into components/gamestage/<name>/ so the import between them resolves the same here and in your app.
